scenario.title: Marginal lane causes recovery storms at Gen4
scenario.description: Lane 5 of link B corrupts ordered sets and data now and then, but only at 16 GT/s (seeded random errors, 0.1 percent per ordered set). Training succeeds, equalization passes, and the link reaches Gen4. From then on receiver errors on lane 5 keep sending the link through Recovery.
scenario.symptom: A device works at full speed and width, but the error log is flooded with corrected errors, and throughput is uneven.
faults: lane 5 of link B corrupts 0.1% of ordered sets at Gen4 only

expected.summary: Link B stays at Gen4 x16 but goes through Recovery many times (flap_count >= 10), every error reported on lane 5; the link never goes down.

scenario.what_to_look_for: Below 16 GT/s link B is quiet. Once it reaches Gen4 (about 26 ms) the swimlanes fill with closely spaced Recovery bars. Every recovery that starts on a port gives the reason "receiver error in L0 on lane 5". The spacing between them is irregular (random errors), unlike the clockwork 3 ms spacing of S07. Run it again with --seed 8: the count changes, the pattern does not.
scenario.what_this_means: When errors cluster on one lane and one rate, the problem is local: one lane of one channel lacks margin at that rate. Equalization can pass and the link can still be marginal, because equalization only has to meet a target once at training time. The fix is usually physical (connector, trace, cable), or reducing the speed as a workaround.
likely_root_causes: One lane with less margin: damaged or contaminated connector pin, via or trace defect, crosstalk hot spot.
Equalization settled on a marginal preset for that lane.
A retimer lane with a problem.
how_to_debug: Check the Lane Error Status register (LaneErrStat in lspci -vvv, Secondary PCI Express capability) to identify the lane.
Run Lane Margining at the Receiver (16 GT/s feature; recent pciutils include a pcilmr tool) and compare lane 5 with the others.
Watch AER correctable errors (Receiver Error) and how fast they increase.
Force Target Link Speed to 8 GT/s and retrain: if the errors stop, the lane lacks margin at 16 GT/s.
Swap slot/cable/riser and see whether the bad lane follows the card or stays with the slot.
mystery_hints: Do the errors point at one lane or at all lanes?
Did the errors exist at 8 GT/s?
scenario.mystery_cause: One lane of the link produces bit errors at 16 GT/s only (marginal lane).
